title: Year boundaries changed the raw seasonal phase-agreement gap between two Great Lakes for 1948-2024 start years
abstract: We tested whether the first month of an annual fit changes the seasonal phase-agreement comparison between Michigan-Huron and Superior. We used coordinated monthly levels, version v2025, and 77 start years from 1948 to 2024. The raw amplitude-weighted agreement gap was -0.0853 for January starts and -0.0321 for October starts. The change was +0.0532, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of +0.0032 to +0.0988. The three-year interval just included zero. Across twelve start months, the raw gap ranged from -0.0904 to +0.0022. A separate linear drift in each window reduced the across-month range from 0.0926 to 0.0245. All fitted-drift simultaneous bands included zero. The comparison thus depends on the annual boundary and drift model. It does not identify true seasonal timing or a physical cause. Overlapping windows, shifted record endpoints, one revised product and sampling assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, retrieval instructions, numerical checks and a figure are included. External monthly records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Michigan-Huron minus Superior amplitude-weighted phase agreement for twelve annual start months. Bars are pointwise conditional 95% intervals. Shading is a simultaneous band within each model. Five-year paired blocks; start years 1948-2024.
